title: Machine-learning tool differentiates asthma and COPD more accurately than physicians
summary: The AC/DC tool, built on 12 electronic health record parameters from more than 400,000 patients, was compared with 180 primary care physicians and 180 pulmonologists on 119 cases from a prospective observational study, with an expert-panel diagnosis (n = 116) as reference. Its average accuracy was superior to primary care physicians (median difference 24%) and to pulmonologists. The test set is small and the reference is a panel diagnosis rather than a gold-standard test.
ai_technology: AC/DC machine learning diagnostic tool using 12 electronic health record parameters
organization: University Medical Center Groningen; University of Groningen; General Practitioners Research Institute
